description: Hi everyone! I am an agronomist and environmental researcher passionate about solving local challenges using data and GIS. I am looking for motivated teammates (developers, data analysts, designers, or creatives) to join me for the NASA Space Apps Challenge in Bukavu. Let's combine our skills in science, technology, and problem-solving to build an impactful, innovative solution together. Join us and let's make a difference
summary:
The Agrsmart project is a geospatial platform dedicated to assessing soil loss and promoting agroecological management in the mountainous Kabare region of South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This initiative addresses severe water erosion that threatens local smallholder food security and the stability of the Lake Kivu watershed.
Agrsmart integrates RUSLE (Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation) soil loss modeling with NASA Earth observation data, including TRMM precipitation records, Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Models, and USGS/NASA optical imagery. The platform relies on a dataset of 4,650 polygons covering 121,774 hectares, optimized by converting Esri JSON to GeoJSON to reduce file sizes by 70%.
Built with Next.js 14, Leaflet, and Mapbox, its interactive Web GIS allows users to visualize parcel-level erosion severity in real time. It also features a two-tier hybrid decision-support system using deterministic pedological rules and community observations to generate 12-month technical roadmaps.
Supported by a Neon Serverless PostgreSQL database and a digitally watermarked document export module, Agrsmart bridges geophysical modeling with practical agronomy to combat erosion, restore soil fertility, and secure sustainable food production across South Kivu and the broader DRC.
details:
Agrsmart

Decision Platform

From Geospatial Data Engineering to an AI-Assisted Agro-Environmental Decision Platform

Initiative & Development Team:
• Grace IlungaMulala Mano: Agritech engineer
• Herve Hwaba MAno: Industrial Chemist
• Elisabeth Lola Mano: Medical Doctor
• Pierre Mano Machumu: Web Developer and ML Engineer

 

1. Territorial Context, Environmental Challenges & Intended Impact

The territory of Kabare, situated in the South Kivu province of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, is characterized by steep highland topography and deeply dissected volcanic ridges (elevations between 1,500 m and 2,200 m above sea level). The equatorial highland climate brings intense, frequent rainfall (1,300 to 1,800 mm/year), generating extreme rainfall erosivity on fragile ferrallitic and volcanic soils that have been severely degraded by demographic pressure, deforestation, and continuous cultivation on slopes exceeding 25%.

This severe soil degradation triggers two catastrophic consequences that Agrsmart is engineered to resolve:

• Preserving Arable Soil & Food Sovereignty: Topsoil depletion directly reduces yields of staple food crops (common beans, maize, and cassava), accelerating rural poverty and malnutrition. By mitigating sheet and rill erosion before irreversible gully formation occurs, Agrsmart protects fertile topsoil and restores sustainable family farm productivity.

• Watershed Protection for Lake Kivu: Massive rill and gully erosion accelerates landslides and catastrophic sediment runoff into downstream river networks emptying into Lake Kivu. Stabilizing these hillsides prevents mudslides, preserves potable water quality, and protects critical transport corridors and regional hydroelectric power stations from siltation.

• Empowering Participatory Governance: Pairing satellite Earth observation with community-driven field logs bridges the gap between scientific institutions and farming communities, fostering grassroots environmental stewardship.

2. Raw Spatial Data Acquisition and Diagnostic Audit

The initial dataset (erosion.geojson, 4.71 MB) was derived from spatial modeling based on the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE): A = R x K x LS x C x P, driven by NASA Earth observations: rainfall erosivity (R) derived from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) satellite series, topographic slope gradient and length (LS) calculated from high-resolution NASA Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) 30 m Digital Elevation Models, soil erodibility (K), cover management (C) from USGS/NASA multispectral imagery, and conservation practice factor (P).

The preliminary technical diagnostic audit identified five major architectural bottlenecks:

• Proprietary Esri JSON Geometry: Geometries were formatted with ArcGIS 'rings' syntax rather than the open GeoJSON standard, making direct rendering impossible in standard web GIS libraries like Leaflet or Mapbox.

• Projected Coordinate System (EPSG:32735): Coordinates were recorded in linear metric units under UTM Zone 35 South, whereas modern web maps require geographic WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) decimal degrees.

• Excessive File Weight for Rural Bandwidth: At 4.71 MB with 15 decimal places of floating-point precision per vertex, loading times over unstable 3G/4G rural mobile connections caused severe timeouts.

• Absence of Temporal Dimensions: The 4,650 polygons represent a static spatial snapshot (an annualized baseline in t/ha/year) with no pre-existing multi-year time-series attributes.

• Descriptive Data Devoid of Prescriptions: The raw attribute table contained only identifiers (OBJECTID, Id), severity class (gridcode 1 to 4), and surface area (Shape_Area in m²), with zero technical advisory or agronomic recommendations.

3. Geospatial Engineering Pipeline and Optimization (grace.py)

To resolve these data constraints, a custom Python pipeline was engineered using the GeoPandas and Shapely libraries (grace.py). The transformation workflow executed the following critical steps:

• Conversion & Topological Repair: Extracted the exterior shell (rings[0]) and interior hole boundaries (rings[1:]). Systematically executed poly.buffer(0) to resolve self-intersecting vertices and non-manifold geometries.

• Geodetic Reprojection: Reprojected all geometries from UTM 35S (EPSG:32735) to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), ensuring pixel-perfect spatial overlay on international satellite basemaps.

• Attribute Calculation & Enrichment: Computed standardized surface areas in hectares (area_ha = Shape_Area / 10,000) and purged redundant Esri database columns.

• Coordinate Precision Truncation & Compression: Rounded coordinate values to 5 decimal places (~1.1 meter ground resolution, ideal for parcel-level soil conservation) and minified JSON whitespace.

• Measured Performance Gains: Reduced file size from 4.71 MB down to 1.41 MB (a 70% decrease in network payload), achieving instantaneous browser rendering on mobile and desktop devices.

4. Web GIS Platform Architecture and Technology Stack

Engineered with a modern web architecture (Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS), Agrsmart delivers speed, graphical clarity, and robust field accessibility across diverse devices:

• Reactive Vector Mapping Engine: Smooth rendering of 4,650 polygons on Leaflet with dynamic opacity controls and a selector for 4 basemaps (Mapbox Outdoors with elevation contours and hillshading, Esri World Topo, OpenStreetMap, Satellite HD).

• Instant Thematic Choropleth Rendering: Dynamic coloring (green for low, yellow for moderate, orange for high, and crimson red for critical), allowing instant visual identification of critical ridgelines and degraded versants.

• Territory-Wide Statistical Dashboard: Macro overview displaying real-time aggregation across the 121,774 mapped hectares, percentage breakdowns, and single-click class isolation filters.

• Advanced Search & Spatial Querying: Instant fly-to and zoom navigation via direct polygon click or search input by parcel ID (#ZoneID), seamlessly opening the technical analysis panel.

Comprehensive Technical Toolset & Environment:

• Programming Languages: TypeScript and JavaScript (ES6+) for type-safe application logic and UI state; Python 3 for data preprocessing and topology engineering; SQL for PostgreSQL relational modeling; HTML5 & CSS3 for responsive layout and print stylesheets.

• Frameworks & UI Libraries: Next.js 14 (App Router) for server-side rendering and edge APIs; React 18 for declarative component state; Tailwind CSS for minimalist modern dark mode styling; Leaflet & React-Leaflet for client-side vector GIS; Lucide React for clean iconography.

• Cloud, AI & Database: Google Gemini API (Gemini-3.6-Flash) for generative advisory; Neon Serverless PostgreSQL for persistent crowdsourced field observations; Vercel Edge Platform for continuous deployment; Git for version control.

5. Two-Tier Agro-Ecological Decision Support Engine

To bridge the gap between raw spatial data and agricultural action, Agrsmart features an intelligent, two-tier hybrid decision engine combining localized agronomic rules with advanced generative AI:

Tier 1: Deterministic Offline Rule Engine (erosionRules.ts)

This client-side engine encodes established soil and water conservation (CES/DRS) standards. As soon as a parcel is selected, the system maps domain-proven practices to its gridcode: crop residue mulching and cover cropping (Mucuna pruriens, Desmodium intortum) for Class 1; contour plowing using an A-frame level and dense vegetative filter strips (Pennisetum purpureum, Vetiver zizanioides) for Class 2; infiltration trenches and nitrogen-fixing agroforestry hedgerows (Calliandra calothyrsus, Leucaena diversifolia) for Class 3; continuous bench terracing, gully head stabilization, and reforestation (Grevillea robusta, Alnus acuminata) for Class 4. This tier guarantees 100% operational availability without requiring network connectivity.

Tier 2: Contextual AI Synthesis via Google Gemini (/api/generate-plan)

When internet connectivity is available and the user clicks 'Generate Technical Plan,' the platform activates a secure serverless API connecting to Google Gemini (multi-model fallback cascade: Gemini 3.6 Flash). The AI agent ingests parcel-specific metrics (polygon ID, exact area in hectares, slope severity, annual soil loss rate) alongside qualitative community field observations. In under one second, Gemini synthesizes a tailored technical report: an executive summary, critical analysis of local field notes, a 12-month phased implementation schedule (Months 1–12: layout, earthworks, planting), recommended agroforestry species, and periodic structure maintenance guidelines.

6. Collaborative Field Observation Network and Cloud Persistence

Agrsmart bridges the gap between top-down GIS modeling and bottom-up participatory monitoring through a collaborative crowdsourcing loop:

• Neon Serverless PostgreSQL Database: The zone_observations table reliably persists field entries (author name, role: agronomist, researcher, farmer, finding type, descriptive comment, and timestamp).

• Real-Time Cartographic Indicators: Parcels with submitted field observations light up with an electric cyan border and display an interactive counter badge '#ZoneID (count)' on the map canvas.

• Offline LocalStorage Redundancy: To guarantee zero data loss during field missions in remote areas with network dropouts, the system seamlessly caches observations in browser localStorage until connectivity is restored.

7. Stakeholder Benefits and Value Proposition

• For Smallholder Farmers: Delivers an early-warning diagnostic before irreversible arable topsoil loss occurs. Rather than abstract warnings, it prescribes multifunctional vegetative barriers (Calliandra calothyrsus, Vetiver zizanioides, Pennisetum purpureum) that stabilize steep slopes while simultaneously providing nutritious livestock fodder and green mulch for staple beans, maize, and cassava crops.

• For Agricultural Extension Agents & Agronomists: Replaces empirical guesswork with standardized engineering guidelines (contour spacing via A-frame leveling, infiltration trench dimensions, planting densities). It serves as an organizing tool for community soil conservation work days.

• For NGOs, Donors, and Public Institutions: Provides transparent, georeferenced data to prioritize public funding and international grants, directing landscape restoration investments to the most critically degraded sub-watersheds.

• For Rural Operations: Boasts a 70% data compression rate, full offline fallback autonomy, and instantaneous client-side rendering on low-cost smartphones over 3G/4G rural networks.

8. Creative Innovation and Critical Engineering Factors

• The 'Satellite-to-Furrow' Translation: Traditional Earth observation models remain locked in academic reports or macro-level government dashboards. Agrsmart creatively translates planetary-scale NASA data down to the individual furrow, giving a smallholder farmer an actionable, 12-month agricultural roadmap.

• Hybrid Intelligence Architecture: To prevent the risks of AI hallucination and network downtime, Agrsmart combines hardcoded deterministic agro-ecological rules with contextual generative AI. The platform seamlessly falls back to local rules if connectivity drops, guaranteeing uninterrupted service in remote hills.

• Rural Infrastructure & Connectivity Constraints: Given unstable cellular networks and expensive mobile data in rural South Kivu, the team engineered offline deterministic fallbacks, local storage caching (localStorage), and aggressive payload compression.

• Agro-Ecological Specifics of the Albertine Rift: Kabare's volcanic and ferrallitic soils on slopes exceeding 25–45% require distinct interventions compared to lowland savannahs. We calibrated recommendations specifically around deep-rooting species (Vetiver, Calliandra) and radical bench terracing.

9. Professional Reporting, Security, and Intellectual Property

• Print-Ready PDF Export Engine (pdfExport.ts): Generates a clean A4 printable report with a single click, featuring a diagonal repeating watermark ('Agrsmart • Grace Mano - Proprietary Intellectual Property'), official disclaimer notice, phased task plan, and direct portfolio link.

• Full Trilingual Internationalization (FR / EN / ES): The entire interface, error handling, basemap guides, and advisory outputs are localized across French, English, and Spanish to facilitate international jury evaluation and donor engagement.

• Proprietary Competition Evaluation License (LICENSE): A source-available legal framework strictly prohibiting unauthorized duplication, forking, or competing commercial deployment, while explicitly granting judges full rights to inspect, analyze, and test the software.

10. Conclusion and Future Perspectives

Agrsmart demonstrates the transformative potential of combining generative AI with modern geospatial engineering to address climate resilience in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. By converting dense, inaccessible GIS data into clear, actionable soil conservation roadmaps for smallholder farmers and agricultural technicians, the platform lays the groundwork for sustainable watershed restoration in Kabare.

Future enhancements will incorporate multi-temporal optical and radar satellite earth observation feeds (Sentinel-2, Landsat) to track seasonal vegetation vigor (NDVI/NDRE indices) and quantitatively monitor the real-world erosion mitigation impact of planted vegetative barriers and radical terraces over time.
